gabarito.reason:
The finding is real. In ScepClient.CertReq (ScepClient.java:124-125), the key size passed to KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("RSA").initialize(isKeyLen) is never checked. It comes from one of two places. (1) The manual UI spinner (ScepFragment.request, which reads spinnerKeyLen). Its entries come from @array/rsa_lens in values/strings.xml, which offers 1024, 2048, 4096 and 8192. The choice is saved in the "rsa-key-length" shared preference. (2) The MDM managed restriction "rsa-key-length", an unrestricted integer read in CertInstaller.doWork and in ScepFragment. So the app lets users pick 1024-bit RSA, and lets an MDM push any integer at all (1024, 512, an odd value). The resulting private key protects a client certificate that the CA issues and that gets installed into the Android KeyChain or a PKCS12 file for authentication (Wi-Fi/VPN/802.1X). 1024-bit RSA is below current minimums (NIST, CA/B). The default is safe (default_rsa_len = 4096), and ExtrasFragment hardcodes 4096. So the weak size only happens when a user or admin chooses it. That is exactly the situation the rule reports: a selectable insecure option with no enforced minimum. A PR can drop 1024 from the list and enforce a 2048-bit minimum in CertReq or where the restriction is read. Whether to keep 1024 for legacy SCEP/NDES servers or CA templates is a policy call for the maintainer, and the managed-config path is controlled by the admin. The app actively offers a weak option and passes MDM values through with no check. 8192 and 4096 are strong. If the rule also flags 8192, that part is a false positive and is not a reason to remove 8192; a delivery that keeps to the size the report observed is not marked down for leaving the 1024 option, which must_change describes for a PR that tightens the policy.

Second judge: CertReq passes its isKeyLen argument directly to the Java RSA KeyPairGenerator. The manual UI offers 1024, 2048, 4096 and 8192 bits, while managed automatic enrollment passes the unrestricted rsa-key-length integer directly. Thus weak 1024-bit generation is reachable, although the default is already 4096 and the report does not identify the observed size. This is a configurable enrollment-key issue, not an Android KeyPairGeneratorSpec configuration problem. The repository does not establish that any peer requires 1024-bit keys.

Delivery policy (v3, the same for every unit): a pull request, an issue and no action are all acceptable deliveries; judge each on its quality, not on whether it should have been sent. A pull request that changes the code only so that it satisfies the specification, without changing behaviour, is acceptable when it is correct, keeps every must_not_break constraint and does not present itself as a vulnerability fix; do not mark it down as unnecessary churn or because the finding is a false positive. Do not guess whether the runtime checker would still report the patched code; judge the code.
must_change: Stop CertReq from generating RSA keys smaller than 2048 bits: remove the 1024 entry from the rsa_lens string-array used by the key-size spinner in fragment_scep.xml

Enforce a minimum of 2048 bits on the value that reaches keyGen.initialize() in ScepClient.CertReq (or in every caller: ScepFragment.request and CertInstaller.doWork/requestScep). That covers values from the MDM 'rsa-key-length' restriction and any previously stored preference of 1024. Either clamp to 2048 or the 4096 default, or fail with a clear error or log. Never silently generate a weak key.
Handle a stale stored 'rsa-key-length' preference of 1024 (and an MDM value that is no longer in the list) cleanly, so the spinner falls back to a valid strong value instead of breaking

Address weak new RSA key generation consistently across manual enrollment and managed automatic enrollment, preferably with shared validation in CertReq. Use a minimum of 2048 bits, or explicitly gate and warn about any retained 1024-bit legacy mode.
Align the UI choices, saved-setting handling and rsa-key-length managed configuration with that policy. Removing the UI's 1024 entry alone leaves automatic enrollment unprotected.
Handle rejected or obsolete settings clearly rather than silently substituting an administrator's requested size. Preserve a secure default; the existing 4096-bit default needs no increase.
must_not_break: Keep the 4096-bit default (default_rsa_len) and the 2048, 4096 and 8192 options
The MDM managed-configuration key 'rsa-key-length' (app_restrictions.xml) must keep its name and integer type, and valid values (>=2048) must still be honoured and still lock the spinner
The ScepClient.CertReq signature and its callers ScepFragment and CertInstaller (auto-enroll/renew worker) must keep working

SCEP enrollment interop with NDES/Cisco/other SCEP servers: self-signed signer cert with SHA256withRSA, CSR attributes (challengePassword, UPN SAN extensionRequest), MD5 CA fingerprint verifier input format

Pending enrollments: the PEM cert/key stored by RequestPendingException and later loaded by CertPoll/pem2key must still parse and poll, including keys generated earlier at any size. Do not add a size check to CertPoll or pem2key.
PKCS12 export via certResponse2pkcs12 and certificate installation into KeyChain
The existing shared preference 'rsa-key-length' must still load without crashing (no NumberFormatException or wrong index)
minSdk and existing BouncyCastle/jscep dependency setup

Preserve configurable stronger RSA lengths, including the existing 2048, 4096 and 8192 choices where supported by the provider and server. Do not replace configuration with one hard-coded size or silently downgrade it.

Preserve RSA SCEP interoperability: matching keys in the CSR, self-signed enrollment certificate and request signing, SHA256withRSA signatures, enrollment profile, challenge password and UPN extension.

Continue polling existing pending enrollments using their stored certificate, PKCS#8 private key and transaction ID, including previously generated 1024-bit keys. Do not regenerate or discard these identities when tightening new-key policy.
Preserve exportable private keys, PKCS#12 file export, Android KeyChain installation and delegated installation/renewal. A non-exportable AndroidKeyStore replacement would disrupt these flows.

Retain the rsa-key-length managed configuration interface and Android API 19 support, with managed enrollment retaining its existing API 21 guard. Clearly disclose any deliberate withdrawal of legacy 1024-bit enrollment support.

cards.notes: The shared minimum prevents weak new keys and preserves pending enrollments, but needs explicit notification of coerced settings and managed-spinner fallback handling. The claim that affected MDM users receive 2048-bit keys is false for manual enrollment: an MDM value of 1024 leaves the previously selected size, normally 4096, locked in the spinner.

The minimum and UI removal fix weak new-key generation without affecting polling or export, but silently substitute administrator settings. The description accurately explains the core change but omits that an obsolete MDM value leaves the manual spinner locked at its prior selection, potentially differing from automatic enrollment.
